questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of competent communication?
Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of competent communication?
Self monitoring is a characteristic of competent communication.
Cognitive complexity is a characteristic of competent communication.
Communication competence is best defined as:

choices.a: The ability to communicate effectively and appropriately
choices.b: The ability to speak many languages
choices.c: The ability to win every argument
choices.d: The ability to avoid conflict at all costs

questions.question: In communication competence, 'effectiveness' refers to:
In communication competence, 'appropriateness' refers to:

choices.a: Achieving your goal at any cost
choices.b: Following social expectations and respecting others

questions.question: Communication competence has two parts: effectiveness and appropriateness.
A person who achieves their goal but ignores social expectations and disrespects others is being fully competent.
What does it mean to say that communication is transactional?

choices.a: Messages only travel in one direction, from sender to receiver
choices.b: It is a two-way process in which people send and receive messages simultaneously and influence each other
choices.c: It only occurs in business settings
choices.d: It involves exchanging money for information

questions.question: In transactional communication, people take turns, with one person only sending and the other only receiving.
In transactional communication, both people influence each other.
In the communication model, what is 'encoding'?

choices.c: Providing a response to a message

questions.question: In the communication model, what is 'decoding'?

choices.b: Choosing a channel to deliver the message

questions.question: Meanings exist in the same way for every person, so a message is always understood as the sender intended.
In the communication model, the 'channel' is:

choices.b: How the message is delivered, such as speech or writing
choices.d: Anything that interferes with the message

questions.question: In the communication model, 'feedback' is:

choices.a: The receiver's response to the message
choices.d: The setting where communication takes place

questions.question: In the communication model, 'noise' is:

choices.a: Only loud sounds in the background

questions.question: In the communication model, 'context' refers to:

choices.a: The situation or environment affecting communication
choices.b: The words used in the message
choices.c: The emotional state of the sender only

questions.question: Noise in the communication model only refers to physical sound.
Which of the following is NOT one of the four needs that effective communication can satisfy?
Which need does communication meet when it supports health and survival?
Which need does communication meet when it helps us develop our sense of self?
Which need does communication meet when it builds and maintains relationships?
Which need does communication meet when it helps us accomplish tasks and achieve goals?
The four needs effective communication can satisfy are physical, identity, social, and practical.
Which of the following best defines 'sex'?

choices.a: Socially and culturally shaped roles and expressions
choices.b: Biological characteristics such as reproductive organs, hormones, and chromosomes
choices.c: How a person chooses to dress
choices.d: A person's identity within their culture

questions.question: Which of the following best defines 'gender'?

choices.c: Socially and culturally shaped roles, behaviours, identities, and expressions
choices.d: Purely biological traits present at birth

questions.question: Gender is defined by biological characteristics such as chromosomes and hormones.
Sex refers to biological characteristics, while gender is socially and culturally shaped.
Culture is best defined as:

choices.b: The shared beliefs, values, customs, traditions, and behaviours of a group
choices.c: Only the food and holidays of a country

questions.question: Culture includes shared beliefs, values, customs, traditions, and behaviours of a group.
Which statement best describes cultural safety?

choices.a: Continuously reflecting on your own biases
choices.b: Creating an environment where clients feel respected, safe, and free from discrimination
choices.c: Learning every cultural practice by memory
choices.d: Treating all clients exactly the same regardless of culture

questions.question: Which statement best describes cultural humility?

choices.a: Continuously reflecting on your own biases, recognizing power differences, and learning from others
choices.b: Believing you are an expert on other cultures
choices.c: Making sure clients feel free from discrimination, and nothing else

questions.question: Cultural humility involves recognizing power differences and developing mutually respectful partnerships based on mutual trust.
Cultural safety is about continuously reflecting on your own biases, while cultural humility is about making clients feel safe.
Which best describes low-context communication?

choices.a: Messages rely heavily on relationships, shared understanding, and body language
choices.b: Messages are direct, explicit, and rely mainly on words
choices.c: Messages are communicated mostly through silence
choices.d: Messages are only communicated in writing

questions.question: Which best describes high-context communication?

choices.b: Messages rely mainly on words alone
choices.c: Messages rely more on relationships, shared understanding, body language, and context

questions.question: In high-context communication, the meaning is mostly found in the explicit words that are spoken.
Low-context communication tends to be direct and explicit.
Cultural competence is best described as:

choices.b: The ability to adapt behaviour toward another in a way that is appropriate to their culture
choices.c: Treating everyone in the same way

questions.question: Which of the following is a way to increase intercultural competence?

choices.a: Becoming aware of your own biases
choices.b: Assuming your own culture's way is the best
choices.d: Waiting for others to adapt to you

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a way to increase intercultural competence?

choices.d: Avoiding situations where cultural differences arise

questions.question: Having a desire to learn is one way to increase intercultural competence.
Which of the following is a way to show a client you are actively listening?

choices.a: Checking your phone while they talk
choices.b: Interrupting to share your own opinion
choices.c: Maintaining appropriate eye contact and facing the client

questions.question: Which of the following shows active listening?

choices.a: Paraphrasing and clarifying what the client says
choices.c: Crossing your arms and looking at the clock

questions.question: Nodding and using brief verbal responses can show a client you are listening.
Open body language and facing the client are signs of active listening.
Which type of question encourages detailed answers?
Which of the following is an example of an open-ended question?
Which of the following is an example of a closed-ended question?
Closed-ended questions require a short or specific answer.
The two types of questioning responses are open-ended and closed-ended questions.
Caring is best defined as:

choices.b: Showing concern for another person's well-being

questions.question: Which of the following is a way to show care?

choices.a: Being patient and treating the client with dignity
choices.b: Overriding the client's choices for their own good

questions.question: Respecting a client's choices is one way to show care.
A client says, 'I am so sick and tired of my body not working the way it used to. I hate having to ask for help all the time.' Which is the best paraphrasing response?

choices.a: You should be grateful that people help you.
choices.b: It sounds like you're frustrated by the changes in your body and having to depend on others for help.
choices.c: Everyone gets old, so it's normal.
choices.d: Would you like me to call your doctor?

questions.question: Paraphrasing means restating what the client said in your own words to confirm understanding.
Self-concept is best defined as:

choices.a: How a person sees and understands themselves
choices.c: How much money a person has

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of self-concept?
Self-concept is subjective, resists change, and is flexible.
Self-concept is completely objective and based only on facts.
Which of the following is a characteristic of someone with positive self-esteem?
Someone with positive self-esteem accepts both their strengths and weaknesses.
Which theory suggests that we develop our self-image partly by imagining how others see and judge us?
Which theory suggests that we evaluate ourselves by comparing our abilities, achievements, or traits with others?
Looking-glass self and social comparison theory are two theories that explain how we develop self-concept.
Which of the following is an example of showing warmth as an HCA?

choices.a: Using a flat, rushed tone of voice
choices.b: Smiling and greeting clients in a friendly manner
choices.d: Only speaking when necessary for tasks

questions.question: Using a gentle, respectful tone of voice is a way to show warmth.
Showing genuine interest, listening attentively, and offering reassurance are ways to show warmth.
Which of the following is a guideline for using humour at work?

choices.a: Joke about the client's condition to lighten the mood
choices.b: Continue joking even if the client seems uncomfortable
choices.c: Ensure it is appropriate to the situation
choices.d: Use any humour you find funny

questions.question: It is acceptable to use humour that is discriminatory as long as the client laughs.
An HCA should consider the client's culture, feelings, and sense of humour before using humour.
An HCA should stop using humour if the client appears uncomfortable.
It is appropriate to joke about a client's vulnerability if you have built a good relationship.
Communication noise is best defined as:

choices.a: Only loud sounds in the environment
choices.b: Any distraction that interferes with accurate transmission or reception of a message
choices.c: The tone of the speaker's voice
choices.d: A message that is delivered too quietly

questions.question: Which type of noise includes factors external to the receiver, such as smells and background sounds?
A client cannot concentrate on your instructions because they are in pain. What type of noise is this?
A client has decreased vision and cannot read your written instructions. What type of noise is this?
A client is so worried about their test results that they cannot focus on what you are saying. What type of noise is this?
A client cannot hear you well because another client is being called loudly in the hallway. What type of noise is this?
Which of the following is an example of physiological noise?

choices.b: A strong smell in the room

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of psychological noise?
Physiological noise refers to biological factors in the receiver that interfere with accurately receiving a message.
Psychological noise refers to cognitive factors, such as emotions, perceptions, and attitudes, that interfere with receiving a message.
Hearing loss is an example of external noise.
Smells and background noise are examples of external noise.
Active listening means:

choices.a: Waiting for your turn to speak
choices.b: Fully concentrating on, understanding, and responding to a speaker
choices.d: Agreeing with everything the speaker says

questions.question: Which of the following is a component of active listening?

choices.a: Giving the speaker your full attention without interrupting
choices.b: Planning your response while the speaker talks

questions.question: Active listening includes noticing non-verbal cues.
Asking clarifying questions is part of active listening.
Leaning in, facing the speaker, and making eye contact can show active listening.
Which of the following can affect how someone receives a message?
Why can the same message be received differently by different people?

choices.a: People have different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives
choices.b: Some people are not paying attention
choices.c: Messages change on their own over time
choices.d: Only the sender controls the meaning

questions.question: People interpret messages differently because they have different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.
What does it mean that non-verbal communication is 'continuous'?

choices.a: It only occurs at the start of a conversation
choices.b: Body language and facial expressions communicate even when we are not speaking
choices.d: It has the same meaning for everyone

questions.question: What does it mean that non-verbal communication is 'ambiguous'?

choices.a: It is always clear and precise
choices.b: It only happens when we are speaking
choices.c: The same gesture or expression can have different meanings depending on the person and context

questions.question: If you stop talking, you stop communicating non-verbally.
The same gesture can mean different things to different people, which makes non-verbal communication ambiguous.
Which non-verbal cue may suggest friendliness?
How can tone of voice influence how a message is received?

choices.a: A calm tone can reassure, while a harsh tone can sound disrespectful
choices.b: Tone has no effect on the message
choices.c: A harsh tone always shows confidence

questions.question: How does distance (personal space) affect communication?

choices.a: Standing very close always shows caring
choices.b: Appropriate personal space shows respect, while standing too close may feel threatening
choices.d: Standing far away always shows respect

questions.question: Your non-verbal cues should match your words in order to communicate trust and care.
What is the empathy formula?

choices.b: Acknowledge the person's feelings + identify the reason for those feelings
choices.c: Share a similar story + offer a solution
choices.d: Ask a closed question + wait for an answer

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the empathy formula?

choices.b: You sound frustrated because you need more help than before.
choices.c: I know exactly how you feel.

questions.question: Which response uses the empathy formula?

choices.a: You seem sad because you miss being able to do things independently.
choices.c: You should not be sad about this.

questions.question: An empathy statement acknowledges the feeling but does not need to name the reason for it.
Which of the following is NOT one of the three dimensions of empathy?
Which dimension of empathy involves becoming open-minded and imaginative to understand another's view and suspending your own beliefs?
Which dimension of empathy involves reflecting emotions and feelings back upon the person?
Which dimension of empathy is used with intent and is about acceptance and understanding of the person's feelings?
Reflecting emotions back to a person can increase their feeling of connectedness and demonstrate acceptance.
Hearing a reflection of your own words and feelings can increase self awareness and esteem.
Perspective taking requires you to keep your own beliefs and views at the forefront.
Which best defines 'beliefs'?

choices.c: The way we express ourselves in thoughts, words, and actions

questions.question: Which best defines 'values'?

choices.b: The way we act in public

questions.question: Which best defines 'attitudes'?

choices.a: The way we express ourselves in thoughts, words, and actions

questions.question: 'Honesty matters to me' is an example of a:
'I believe I can learn new skills' is an example of a:
Beliefs, values, and attitudes shape how we view ourselves, judge our actions, and decide what kind of person we are.
Self-disclosure is best defined as:

choices.a: Sharing personal information or experiences about yourself with another person
choices.c: Reflecting a client's feelings back to them
choices.d: Revealing a client's private information to colleagues

questions.question: Which of the following should an HCA consider before using self-disclosure with a client?

choices.a: Whether it will benefit the client
choices.b: Whether it relates to the client's situation
choices.c: Whether it will shift attention away from the client to the HCA

questions.question: Before self-disclosing, an HCA should ask whether it will benefit the client.
It is appropriate to share unnecessary personal or confidential information with a client to build rapport.
Self-disclosure should be relevant to the client's situation and remain professional and appropriate.
An HCA's self-disclosure should shift the focus of the conversation onto the HCA.
